subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin refused to grant a question, stating the listener did not donate a book.
source_quote: You don't get a question. You did not donate a book.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin received the description of Philemon as a man who had been hoping someone would say exactly those words.
source_quote: Thorin received this information like a man who has been hoping someone would say exactly these words.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz observed that there were apparently two famous people in the party.
source_quote: Daz observed that there were apparently two famous people in the party.

subject: First Reader
fact: The First Reader assigned scholars, with Zalthir getting the Jimjar thread, which dovetailed with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.
source_quote: The First Reader assigned scholars. Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific.

subject: Zalthir's Jimjar thread
fact: The Jimjar thread is unresolved and tied to an avowed named Khell-Vire whose specific interest remains unstated beyond being about 'me' in particular.
source_quote: Zalthir got the Jimjar thread — which apparently dovetailed neatly with an avowed named Khell-Vire who wanted to learn about something specific. The First Reader clarified: not about the party generally, but about *me* in particular.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud beat Protanther at chess with an unexpected, definitive move that caused the world to shift.
source_quote: Stroud beat Protanther at chess. ... Stroud rolled — and it landed perfectly. Definitively. The kind of thing that doesn't just work, it *announces* itself. Protanther was so stunned he joined the alliance. The world shifted because someone who didn't know what they were doing did the exact right thing at the exact right moment.

subject: Stroud
fact: Stroud's chess move became known as 'Stroud's Gambit,' a term that redefined a scholarly field.
source_quote: And then, because I couldn't help it, and because the phrase had been sitting in the back of my mind since we started this journey and I'd never had the right audience for it: 'Stroud's Gambit.'

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth expressed outrage at the First Reader for not informing him about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.
source_quote: I cannot believe you did not tell me about the arrival of a cleric of Bahamut.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth has a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts, a previously quiet, small area of study.
source_quote: He had, he explained breathlessly, a decades-long specialty in half-orc Bahamut converts. Which had, until recently, been a quiet, small area of study. A niche. Something he'd pursued with quiet dedication while the rest of the academic world found more fashionable problems.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth grabbed the speaker's hand and practically dragged them.
source_quote: He grabbed my hand and practically dragged me.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker let Vareth drag them because they were curious and had questions of their own.
source_quote: I let him. I was curious, and also I had questions of my own.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker believes it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to take over the world, but has not moved into that phase yet.
source_quote: You have to understand," I said, with the measured cadence I use when I'm testing someone, "that it is traditional for clerics of Bahamut to want to try to take over the world. But I haven't moved into that phase yet.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth is eager to test out theories about Bahamut half-orc conversions and is thrilled to receive new information.
source_quote: This is all fascinating! I have so many theories I wish to test out.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker completed Vareth's thought by saying, 'It truly was legendary.'
source_quote: I felt it coming together and finished the thought for him: 'It truly was legendary.'

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth reacted with surprise, recognition, and delight upon hearing the term 'Stroud's Gambit.'
source_quote: Vareth stopped. His expression went through several stages very quickly — surprise, recognition, something that looked almost like delight at receiving a gift he hadn't known he wanted. '*Oh.* Oh! Well, that's not how — this is all novel news! I can't wait to take advantage of it!'

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker said, 'It's all part of the plan,' in response to Vareth's enthusiasm.
source_quote: Oh," I said, as warmly as I could manage, "it's all part of the plan.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's name was pulled into a discussion about Daz's habit of citing Malfire at every opportunity.
source_quote: Somewhere in the background, the rest of the party had begun debating Daz's habit of citing Malfire at every available opportunity. I heard Grygum's name pulled into the discussion — *Grygum*, not me, which is how I know the sentence was reconstructed after the fact

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker describes the party's dynamic as being sick of each other but still together.
source_quote: Yeah," I said, when someone turned to me for confirmation, "it's like we're kind of sick of each other, but somehow still together, yeah.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker cited 'Malfire said in Volume 3' as a response to the group's conversation.
source_quote: And then, because the opportunity was simply too good: 'As Malfire said in Volume 3.'

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker finds comfort in the idea that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.
source_quote: I had the particular comfort of knowing that sometimes the person who doesn't know what they're doing walks into the right room and everything clicks.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker took notes on theological documents, the prayer book, and accumulated evidence from months in the Underdark.
source_quote: I took notes. It's what I do.

subject: Speaker's conversion
fact: The speaker's conversion and its meaning in the broader theological landscape remain unexplored and unresolved.
source_quote: About Bahamut's intentions, about what my conversion meant in the broader theological landscape, about why Vareth's previously obscure field had become a flood. I didn't know what I was going to find.

subject: Malfire's citations
fact: Daz's habit of citing Malfire has become an ambient weather condition for the party, but the source and meaning of these citations remain unstated beyond their frequency.
source_quote: We had been through enough together that the citations had become a kind of ambient weather condition, something you adapted to rather than fought.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker said, 'I almost feel like they should be giving us books,' while observing scholars being pointed at them like a hospitality service they hadn't paid for.
source_quote: What I did say, looking at the assembled scholars being pointed at us like a hospitality service we hadn't paid for: 'I almost feel like they should be giving us books.'

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker said, 'I'm feeling,' to no one in particular, 'in demand here.'
source_quote: I'm feeling," I said, to no one in particular, "in demand here.

subject: Speaker
fact: The speaker looked at Vareth, and Vareth looked at the speaker, with Vareth's eyes expressing the look of a man who has found a very rare specimen in the wild.
source_quote: I looked at him. He looked at me. His eyes had the expression of a man who has found a very rare specimen in the wild.

subject: Vareth
fact: Vareth said, 'And I do have something I can share with you?' after the speaker's statement about Bahamut clerics.
source_quote: And I do have something I can share with you?
